key_insight: The paper shows that reinforcement learning with metacognitive feedback can teach LLMs to express uncertainty more faithfully instead of sounding overconfident. In simple terms, the model learns to better know and say what it does not know.
problem_solved: It addresses the common LLM failure mode where models hallucinate with high confidence, fail to recognize the limits of their knowledge, and give misleading uncertainty signals. This undermines reliability, calibration, and trust in real-world use.
method: Use reinforcement learning to optimize model behavior based on metacognitive feedback rather than only answer accuracy.
Train the model to monitor its own confidence and align expressed uncertainty with actual performance.
Encourage responses that reflect knowledge boundaries, so the model can abstain or hedge appropriately when unsure.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a path toward more trustworthy and calibrated LLMs that can communicate uncertainty honestly. That can improve safety, user trust, and decision-making in applications where overconfidence is costly.
visual_elements: Before/after comparison of overconfident vs calibrated model responses

paper_title: Reinforcement Learning with Metacognitive Feedback Elicits Faithful Uncertainty Expression in LLMs
paper_authors: Gabrielle Kaili-May Liu, Avi Caciularu, Gal Yona, Idan Szpektor, Arman Cohan
